title: Paired Burn
summary: Same people, two time points: the paired t-test, why it's a one-sample test on differences, and how it handles missing pairs.
hints: `t.test(survey$anxiety_pre, survey$anxiety_post, paired = TRUE)`: two columns, not a formula.
`diffs <- survey$anxiety_pre - survey$anxiety_post`, then `t.test(diffs)`. Missing posts give NA differences, which t.test() drops.
`n_pairs <- sum(!is.na(diffs))`, `mean_diff <- mean(diffs, na.rm = TRUE)`, and d_z is `mean_diff / sd(diffs, na.rm = TRUE)`.
